title.value: The Myelin-Weighted Connectome in Parkinson’s Disease
title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the beginning of the paper which states "RESEARCH ARTICLE: The Myelin-Weighted Connectome in Parkinson’s Disease".
title.quote:
RESEARCH ARTICLE
The Myelin-Weighted Connectome in Parkinson’s Disease

analysis.description: The paper investigates the myelin content changes in Parkinson’s Disease using myelin-sensitive MRI metrics, building a myelin-weighted connectome to explore alterations associated with PD and their relationship with clinical scores.

type.justification: The paper involves empirical studies analyzing myelin content changes in individuals with Parkinson’s Disease using imaging techniques and statistical analysis tools.
type.quote: In this study, we have shown that the myelin-weighted connectome was able to identify alterations of the myelin content along connections that were mostly emerging from the basal ganglia.

name.justification: The paper focuses on analyzing changes in brain myelin content using MR imaging techniques to construct a myelin-weighted connectome.
name.quote: In particular, a number of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) studies have demonstrated alterations in brain network architecture in various cortical and subcortical systems.

name.justification: The research investigates neurological conditions, specifically Parkinson’s Disease, and the spread of related neuropathologies.
name.quote: Neurodegeneration in patients with PD with rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD; PDRBD) follows the Braak model (“bottom-up”) of disease progression.

name.justification: The focus is on understanding and mapping neurological degeneration associated with Parkinson’s Disease.
